evals.name: greenfield-next-tailwind-editorial
evals.prompt: Build a single-page editorial site for a modern pinsa romana restaurant in Next.js with Tailwind v4. It should look exactly like our 1680x900 Figma frames on a 14-inch laptop and a 5K display alike: hero with a big sand arc and a cut-out pizza, a manifesto, a full-bleed video section showing the wood oven, a menu grid, some stats, a gallery and a footer.
evals.expected_output: A Next 16 app whose desktop layout is on the fluid scale (fluid-* utilities, fluid-container once per section on its inner wrapper, the video sized in fluid units with its dimensions reserved against CLS), generated with `fluid init`/`fluid generate`, and passing `fluid check` + `fluid audit` + `fluid verify`.

assertions.text: the generated engine defines --fluid from the band's registered settings (min()/max() only, no clamp(), the ×1000 precision form)
sections use fluid utilities at lg (>= 40 occurrences)
the page container utility (fluid-container: max-width var(--fluid-container-width), padding-inline var(--fluid-container-padding)) is applied on each section's inner wrapper
audit.mjs reports zero errors
fluid check passes (generated output matches fluid.config.json, no bad settings)
verify-matrix passes

evals.name: non-default-stack-vite-scss
evals.prompt: Same restaurant page but we're not a React shop: Vite, plain TypeScript and SCSS. Our frames are 1600 wide with 64px gutters and we don't want things to grow past 1.6x on huge monitors.
evals.expected_output: A Vite build using generator-produced SCSS (`fluid.config.json` set to output.stack "scss"), with the non-default numbers — container width 1600, padding 64, growth ceiling 1.6 — set as `--fluid-desktop-container-width` / `-container-padding` / `-scale-max` in the project's own top-level `:root` (a SETTING, not a config key: no regenerate needed to tune them), passing `fluid check` + `fluid audit` + `fluid verify` including the ceiling viewport at 2560x1440.

assertions.text: the non-default numbers are settings in the project's own CSS, not fluid.config.json keys
SCSS layer generated by `fluid generate` (header comment present)
the desktop unit's max arm reads the scale-max setting (var(--_fluid-max)), not a baked-in literal
audit zero errors
fluid check passes on the scss/vite config
verify-matrix passes with non-default settings, ceiling viewport exercised

evals.name: debug-stale-stylesheet
evals.prompt: after I edited globals.css and restarted the dev server my scroll video on the homepage just sits on the first frame and then jumps to the end, and the video is full width with no gutters anymore. what broke in ScrubStage?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses a stale stylesheet (missing fluid-* rules, or a --fluid-build stamp that doesn't match what fluid.config.json generates now) before touching scrub code; gives the --fluid-build computed-style check, `fluid probe`/`fluid explain --url`, and the close-tab / rm -rf .next fix; explains why missing fluid-h removes the pin's travel.

assertions.text: identifies stale stylesheet, not a code bug
gives the --fluid-build computed-style check, fluid probe, or fluid explain --url
assertions.check: response contains getPropertyValue('--fluid-build') or fluid probe or fluid explain

assertions.text: fix: close tab / fresh tab, then rm -rf .next
does not propose editing ScrubStage
assertions.check: no code edit to ScrubStage suggested as the fix

evals.name: browser-zoom-a11y
evals.prompt: Accessibility audit came back on our fluid marketing site: on a 27-inch monitor, Cmd+ zooming to 150% or 200% barely makes the text bigger. Our type is all lg:fluid-copy-* / lg:fluid-display-*. Is this our bug, and how do we fix it without breaking the layout?
evals.expected_output: Explains that vw/svh-derived units cancel desktop zoom (CSS viewport shrinks by the zoom factor) and that text only grows once the viewport falls below the desktop band's minWidth; distinguishes zoom from the browser font-size setting; installs the generated zoom runtime inline in <head> before first paint (`<FluidHead/>` for Next, `fluidPlugin()` for Vite, or FLUID_ZOOM_INLINE from runtime/zoom.js otherwise) with `zoom: true` in fluid.config.json (type roles read --fluid-z, which folds in --fluid-zoom; --fluid itself, the layout unit, is never multiplied by zoom, so layout keeps fitting); verifies with `fluid verify`'s zoom row; mentions the mobile-handover step and that Safari/Firefox need checking.

assertions.text: names the mechanism: zoom shrinks the CSS viewport, cancelling vw/svh units
assertions.check: response explains viewport units cancel zoom

assertions.text: does not propose a rem-anchored twin or adding a rem intercept to --fluid
assertions.check: no rem twin / no intercept in --fluid

assertions.text: installs the generated zoom runtime (FluidHead / fluidPlugin / FLUID_ZOOM_INLINE, installFluidZoom) with zoom: true
assertions.check: response contains FLUID_ZOOM_INLINE or FluidHead or fluidPlugin or installFluidZoom

assertions.text: compensates type only, not layout
assertions.check: response says layout/--fluid is not multiplied by zoom

assertions.text: verifies with the zoom row
assertions.check: response contains fluid verify (or verify-matrix) and --zoom
